name: Golf Club of Oregon Pro Shop

nadir.desc: The property consists of a cluster of single-story buildings with green roofs located adjacent to a paved parking lot|Multiple vehicles are parked in the lot|Golf course fairways, greens, and scattered trees extend across the southern portion of the site|A railroad track runs along one edge of the property|Road access is available from NW Springhill Dr.

alpha.desc: The front approach to the property is heavily screened by dense trees along the roadway|Portions of the golf course terrain and open grassy areas are visible beyond the tree line|The main buildings and parking lot are largely obscured from this angle by vegetation.

bravo.desc: The left side of the property shows the paved parking lot and the cluster of green-roofed buildings|Multiple vehicles are present in the lot|A railroad track runs along one edge|Open golf course areas and scattered trees extend beyond the developed zone|Road access is visible along the perimeter.

charlie.desc: The rear of the property shows the full layout of the parking lot, green-roofed buildings, and surrounding golf course terrain|Fairways, greens, and tree clusters are visible across the open areas|The railroad track borders one side of the site|Circulation space exists around the buildings and parking lot.

delta.desc: The right side of the property shows extensive golf course fairways and tree lines leading toward the parking lot and green-roofed buildings in the distance|The railroad track runs along the outer edge|Open grassy and maintained turf areas dominate the view, with the pro shop complex visible at the far end of the site.

considerations: Vehicle access is available from NW Springhill Dr into a paved parking lot adjacent to a cluster of green-roofed buildings. Multiple vehicles occupy the lot. The site is part of an active golf course with fairways, greens, and scattered trees extending across large open areas. A railroad track borders one edge of the property. The developed area (pro shop and related structures) is relatively compact, while the surrounding course provides extensive open space. Neighboring uses include a school and residential properties.
clarifications: Which of the green-roofed buildings is the primary pro shop entrance? Are there designated fire lanes or emergency vehicle access routes within the parking lot? Is vehicle or cart path access available from the pro shop area directly onto the golf course? Do any gates or barriers control access between the parking lot and the course? Are maintenance or storage buildings on the site accessible independently from the main pro shop?
